title: Unapproved Kerberos Constrained-Delegation Ticket Paths
exclusions: Detects successful Windows Security event 4769 service-ticket requests whose `TransitedServices` field is populated, indicating constrained Kerberos delegation, and whose exact transited-service, requested-service, and client-address path lacks a valid governed approval. It does not prove credential theft, ticket forgery, pass-the-ticket, compromise, malicious intent, backend access success, authorization outcome, or data access. It does not detect unconstrained delegation, delegation configuration changes, S4U2self alone, NTLM fallback, missing KDC audit events, or a malicious path incorrectly approved in the lookup. Resource-based and account-based constrained delegation require separate configuration inventory but can both produce S4U2proxy use. The deployment-selected `index=windows`, five-minute schedule, lookup schema, and notification severity are local choices. Documentation review created no runtime, identity-SME, or production evidence.
evidence: Retain effective Kerberos Service Ticket Operations audit policy; KDC and domain inventory; raw successful 4769 XML; Windows/add-on versions; governed exports of account-based `msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo` and resource-based `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity`/`PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount`; versioned `windows_kerberos_delegation_paths.csv` with owner, approver, ticket, validity, and source revision; `windows_unapproved_constrained_delegation_paths` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, and rows; source-health results; alert actions; investigations; and dated approved/unapproved, case, IPv4-mapped, failure-code, missing-field, duplicate, late-arrival, lookup-boundary, and expiry tests. Each finding preserves KDC, event/index time, record ID, domain/user, requested service and SID, exact transited-services value, client address/port, ticket options/encryption type, status, logon GUID, provider/source/type, approval decision, and disposition. This editorial review generated none of those deployment artefacts.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index and lookup, ingest a successful Security event 4769 from `host=dc-lab-01` with `Status=0x0`, `TargetUserName=alice`, `ServiceName=filesvc$`, `TransitedServices=http/app-lab-01.example.test`, and `IpAddress=::ffff:192.0.2.25`. Omit an approval for normalized tuple `http/app-lab-01.example.test,filesvc$,192.0.2.25`; expect exactly one row with `approval_state=unapproved`. Add an approval whose exclusive expiry equals the event epoch and rerun; expect the row because an event at expiry is not approved.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest the same 4769 with one unique lookup row whose exact normalized tuple matches, `valid_from_epoch` is at or before the event, `valid_until_epoch` is after it, `enabled=1`, and owner/approver/ticket are populated; expect zero rows. Also expect zero for successful 4769 with `TransitedServices=-`, failed 4769 with `Status=0x6`, event 4768, a 4769 from the Application channel, and an approved event one second before exclusive expiry. Base/raw searches must still retain every approved event.

dataSources: Primary source: Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing event 4769 from the Security channel on every in-scope domain controller/KDC, collected as `sourcetype=WinEventLog` or `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742). Microsoft documents 4769 as a Kerberos service-ticket request and `Transited Services` as the list of SPNs requested when constrained delegation was used. Required fields are `EventCode`, `Status`, `TargetUserName`, `TargetDomainName`, `ServiceName`, `ServiceSid`, `IpAddress`, `IpPort`, `TicketOptions`, `TicketEncryptionType`, `TransitedServices`, and preferably `LogonGuid`, `EventRecordID`, provider/channel, and ticket hashes where supported. Governance sources are read-only Active Directory exports of classic and resource-based delegation configuration plus the approved-path lookup.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) for KDC Security event collection/extraction. A deployment-owned Kerberos security-content app must supply the exact `windows_kerberos_delegation_paths.csv` lookup, delegation inventory, saved search, source-health checks, fixtures, dashboard, and response runbook.
spl:
index=windows source IN ("WinEventLog:Security","XmlWinEventLog:Security") sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog","XmlWinEventLog") EventCode=4769 Status="0x0" TransitedServices!="-"
| eval transited_services=lower(trim(mvjoin(TransitedServices,";"))), service_name=lower(trim(ServiceName)), client_address=lower(replace(trim(IpAddress),"^::ffff:","")), delegated_user=lower(TargetDomainName."\\".TargetUserName), event_epoch=floor(_time)
| where len(transited_services)>0 AND len(service_name)>0 AND len(client_address)>0
| lookup windows_kerberos_delegation_paths.csv transited_services service_name client_address OUTPUTNEW approval_id enabled valid_from_epoch valid_until_epoch owner approver ticket
| eval enabled=tonumber(enabled), valid_from_epoch=tonumber(valid_from_epoch), valid_until_epoch=tonumber(valid_until_epoch), approval_state=if(isnotnull(approval_id) AND enabled=1 AND valid_from_epoch<=event_epoch AND event_epoch<valid_until_epoch AND len(owner)>0 AND len(approver)>0 AND len(ticket)>0,"approved","unapproved")
| where approval_state="unapproved"
| table _time host delegated_user TargetUserName TargetDomainName service_name ServiceName ServiceSid transited_services TransitedServices client_address IpAddress IpPort TicketOptions TicketEncryptionType Status LogonGuid RequestTicketHash ResponseTicketHash EventRecordID approval_state approval_id owner approver ticket source sourcetype _indextime
| sort 0 - _time host EventRecordID
description: Returns one row for each successful KDC 4769 event that carries a constrained-delegation transited-service chain but does not match an enabled, complete, time-valid approval for the exact normalized transited service, requested service, and client address. The row grain is the service-ticket request, not a volume threshold or proof that the backend accepted the ticket.
value: Constrained delegation legitimately lets a front-end service obtain a backend ticket on a user's behalf, making broad anomaly counts noisy. Comparing observed S4U2proxy paths with a reviewed least-privilege path inventory exposes new or expired delegation use while retaining the user, service, KDC, source, encryption, and ticket context needed to distinguish application rollout from unauthorized lateral access.
implementation: Enable Kerberos Service Ticket Operations auditing on every KDC, collect the Security channel in a qualified classic or XML format, and verify successful 4769 extraction including `TransitedServices`. Build an exact, nonoverlapping approved-path lookup from tested application flows and Active Directory delegation configuration. Save the SPL as `windows_unapproved_constrained_delegation_paths`, run it every five minutes with a measured overlap and durable event checkpoint, and investigate every unmatched or expired path; operate KDC coverage and configuration-change detections separately.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — Kerberos Delegation Paths`: show KDC/source health first; unapproved paths by transited service, requested service, client address, delegated user, application owner, and age; approved-path use and paths unused for review; first/last seen; encryption type; lookup expiry; and ticket/change disposition. A directed graph may draw `transited_services -> service_name`, but must label client address, user, event count, and exact time range and must not infer a host from an account/SPN without authoritative resolution. Drill down to raw 4769 XML, lookup row/revision, AD delegation inventory, nearby KDC events, front-end/backend application logs, and incident record. Missing KDC data is unknown, never zero delegation.
schema: Microsoft Windows Security event 4769 plus deployment-governed exact delegation-path approval lookup
dataModelAcceleration: The Windows add-on maps event 4769 into normalized models, but the Authentication CIM does not guarantee preservation of `TransitedServices`, exact requested service/SID, status, ticket fields, lookup validity, and event identity needed for this detector. The primary search therefore uses raw Microsoft fields. An accelerated summary is acceptable only if it preserves those fields and passes event-for-event parity; generic authentication counts cannot establish constrained delegation.

knownFalsePositives:
A row is a real successful constrained-delegation ticket path that governance did not approve at the event time; it is not automatically adversary activity.

1. **New application deployment** — A front-end begins delegating to a backend before the path inventory is published. Confirm application release, exact front-end identity/address, backend service account/SPN, test evidence, data owner, least-privilege review, and ticket. Add approval only after review; never suppress by service class alone.

2. **Load balancer, proxy, cluster, or failover address change** — The same application path can originate from a new node or address. Validate VIP/SNAT behavior, cluster membership, DNS/SPN registration, application logs, and why client address is stable enough for identity. Version exact nodes or an explicitly governed address representation rather than wildcarding.

3. **Service-account or SPN migration** — Rotation, gMSA adoption, rename, backend move, or duplicate-SPN cleanup can change `ServiceName` or `TransitedServices`. Compare old/new AD objects, SPNs, delegation properties, cutover window, owner, and removal plan for obsolete rights.

4. **Disaster recovery or site failover** — A standby front-end may invoke an approved backend only during an exercise or outage. Require DR event, exact hosts/addresses/path, exclusive expiry, incident commander, and post-failback confirmation.

5. **Troubleshooting or vendor support test** — Engineers can deliberately exercise KCD/RBCD while diagnosing a second-hop failure. Verify named operator, test user, front/back services, source address, approved window, captured traces, and immediate expiry.

6. **Lookup deployment lag or search-head inconsistency** — A valid row may be absent or stale on one search head. Compare lookup checksum/revision, bundle replication, dispatch peer, effective CSV, and publication time. Treat inconsistent governance data as content health, not as proof the event was approved.

7. **IPv4-mapped IPv6 representation** — Windows may emit `::ffff:192.0.2.25` while inventory stores `192.0.2.25`. The SPL normalizes only that prefix. Verify raw address, normalization test, and no ambiguous hostname/NAT conversion.

8. **Multiple transited services or representation variance** — Case, ordering, or delimiters can differ in observed chains. Preserve raw `TransitedServices`, normalize only documented/tested representation, and approve the exact semantic path. Do not sort or truncate a chain merely to obtain a match.

**Safe suppression:** use `lookup windows_kerberos_delegation_paths.csv` with exact `transited_services,service_name,client_address`, unique `approval_id`, `enabled=1`, inclusive `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, and ticket. Reject duplicate keys, overlapping windows, wildcards, blank addresses, regex rows, open-ended expiry, and whole-service/domain exceptions. Approval suppresses notification only; raw events, lookup match, and source/configuration health remain retained.
mitreAttack: N/A (ATT&CK has no discrete constrained-delegation-use technique; a successful 4769 S4U2proxy path alone does not establish stolen/forged ticket use, pass-the-ticket, valid-account abuse, or adversary intent)
hardware: Windows Active Directory domain controllers acting as Kerberos KDCs, plus governed Windows or non-Windows front-end/back-end services represented in the delegation inventory. MIT Kerberos-only realms, Entra ID-only authentication, NTLM, unconstrained delegation, and KDCs whose 4769 schema/extraction has not been qualified require separate controls.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft 4769, KCD/RBCD, S4U2proxy, and delegation-attribute documentation; Splunk Microsoft Windows add-on source/CIM documentation; and MITRE's current Pass-the-Ticket definition used to reject the prior direct T1550.003 claim; KDC auditing, fields, AD inventory, lookup, SPL, fixtures, alerting, dashboard, scale, and response were specified but not executed or Kerberos/identity/Splunk-SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: Event 4769 can be high-volume on KDCs. The detector narrows to successful events with populated TransitedServices before an exact lookup, but retention and dispatch cost scale with domain authentication traffic; prefiltering must preserve every relevant event and lookup parity.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and detection contract

Assign Kerberos/AD, application, service-account, network, Splunk data/content, detection, and incident owners. Inventory every domain/KDC, front-end service identity and address, target service account/SPNs, delegated users/classes, classic constrained-delegation `msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo` values, RBCD `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity` security descriptors or `PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount`, application owner, environment, approval, and validity. Configuration permission is not observed use, and observed use is not proof the configuration is safe; retain both.

Microsoft defines S4U2proxy as a service obtaining a ticket to another service on behalf of a user. Event 4769 is generated on the KDC when a Kerberos service ticket is requested. Microsoft documents `Transited Services` as the list of SPNs requested if constrained delegation was used. Therefore this detector scopes successful 4769 events with a non-hyphen value and compares the observed path with explicit governance. It does not infer constrained delegation from ticket volume, `krbtgt`, LDAP/CIFS naming, or a populated client name alone.

The prior T1550.003 mapping is removed. MITRE defines Pass the Ticket as use of stolen Kerberos tickets without the password. A normal KDC-issued S4U2proxy request can occur with no stolen or injected ticket, so an unapproved path is security-relevant but does not by itself satisfy T1550.003, T1558, or T1078. Add an ATT&CK mapping in downstream content only when additional evidence establishes that behavior.

## Step 1 — Enable and verify KDC auditing

Enable **Advanced Audit Policy Configuration > Account Logon > Audit Kerberos Service Ticket Operations** for Success on every in-scope domain controller using governed Group Policy. Record effective policy, GPO/RSoP, KDC inventory, OS build, January 2025-or-later event-schema update status where applicable, channel size/retention, and collection assignment. Event 4769 can be high volume; size Security logs and forwarding capacity from measured rates, not an assumed default.

In an isolated domain/application lab, perform one known KCD or RBCD request and inspect Event Viewer **Windows Logs > Security** raw XML on the KDC. Verify provider, channel, event ID/version, status `0x0`, account/domain, service name/SID, client address/port, ticket options/encryption type, transited services, logon GUID, event record ID, and new request/response ticket hashes if the OS version emits them. Record whether a hyphen or blank represents no constrained delegation in that exact extraction. Do not test by granting production delegation to a new principal.

Create KDC/source health independent of this detector. Report inventory KDCs missing the Security feed, audit-policy drift, channel overwrite/clear, forwarding delay/drop, wrong source/type, malformed event, and missing mandatory fields. Absence of 4769 rows is never proof that no delegation occurred.

## Step 2 — Collect and extract with the Windows add-on

Use Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742). Qualify either classic source `WinEventLog:Security` with `sourcetype=WinEventLog` or XML source `XmlWinEventLog:Security` with `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`; the SPL accepts both. Place `inputs.conf` in a deployment app's `local` layer. Send events to deployment-selected `index=windows` or change the explicit index under RBAC review. Splunk Cloud receives the feed from customer-managed collection infrastructure.

Compare raw XML to extracted `EventCode, Status, TargetUserName, TargetDomainName, ServiceName, ServiceSid, IpAddress, IpPort, TicketOptions, TicketEncryptionType, TransitedServices, LogonGuid`, and event identity for every supported OS/rendering/add-on combination. Microsoft expanded 4769 in 2025, so optional hash and encryption-support fields must be treated as versioned—not fabricated when absent. Do not alias `service_name` back into `ServiceName` without a field-by-field parity test; CIM normalization can change semantics.

The SPL removes only an IPv4-mapped IPv6 `::ffff:` prefix and lowercases/trims exact strings. It does not resolve DNS, expand an account into all SPNs, split a chain into guessed hops, or map NAT to an original host. If `TransitedServices` is multivalue, it joins values in retained order with `;`; qualify that behavior with real events before production.

## Step 3 — Build a governed approval inventory

Generate a read-only AD configuration export on a secure management host using the ActiveDirectory module and a least-privilege reader. For classic KCD, capture the delegating user/computer/service account, `msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo`, `TrustedToAuthForDelegation`/relevant account-control state, object SID/GUID, SPNs, domain, and collection time. For RBCD, capture each backend account's `PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount` or decode the `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity` descriptor into principal SIDs/names while preserving the raw descriptor hash. Microsoft documents that RBCD stores the access-control decision on the backend resource account.

Configuration does not necessarily yield the exact 4769 display strings or client address. Establish approved observed tuples during application testing and tie each to the AD configuration objects. Create `windows_kerberos_delegation_paths.csv` with exact lowercase `transited_services,service_name,client_address`, unique approval ID, integer enabled flag, inclusive start, exclusive expiry, application/environment, front-end and backend identities, owner, approver, ticket, AD snapshot revision, and review date.

Reject blank keys, wildcards, regular expressions, broad subnets, duplicate keys, overlapping effective windows, start at/after expiry, invalid epochs, unknown owners, missing tickets, and expiry beyond policy. Publish atomically and verify checksum/bundle consistency on every search head. A separate health search must alert on invalid/expired/overlapping rows and observed AD configuration with no reviewed path.

## Step 4 — Create and understand the primary SPL

Save the sidecar SPL as `windows_unapproved_constrained_delegation_paths`. The base term fixes index, Security sources/types, event 4769, success status, and non-hyphen transited services. Normalization creates exact lookup keys and integer event epoch. The `where` clause rejects events missing any key; a separate data-quality search must report them so malformed telemetry cannot become silent approval.

`lookup` returns approval metadata for the exact tuple. The result is approved only when one governed row exists, `enabled=1`, start is at/before the event, event is strictly before expiry, and owner/approver/ticket are nonempty. Every other observed path is returned. Trigger on result count greater than zero; there is no `count>50` threshold. Fifty approved requests are expected behavior, while one novel path can be material.

Validate lookup uniqueness before dispatch because a CSV lookup with duplicate input keys can yield ambiguous selection. If temporal history requires multiple nonoverlapping rows for one tuple, use a governed KV collection or enrich candidates then evaluate all matching windows deterministically; do not rely on CSV row order.

Authentication CIM can support broad Kerberos reporting, but it does not guarantee this detector's transited chain or approval fields. Do not replace the SPL with `tstats count by user,src,dest`. A summary index must preserve raw event key, exact path, status, user/service/SID, ticket context, approval revision, and source health and must pass event-for-event tests.

## Step 5 — Schedule, deduplicate, and test

Measure p99 KDC-to-index delay. Run every five minutes over a locally measured overlap, commonly ten minutes only if evidence supports it. Maintain a durable checkpoint keyed by KDC/provider/channel/event record ID and event time; use ticket hashes as additional correlation where versioned fields exist, not as a cross-version requirement. Never `dedup user service_name client_address`, because legitimate repeated tickets are separate evidence.

Run the exact control fixtures with fixed epochs. Add cases for lowercase/uppercase SPNs, whitespace, scalar/multivalue transited services, IPv4 and mapped IPv6, native IPv6, missing address/service/chain, `Status=0x0` versus failures, exact start, one second before expiry, at expiry, disabled row, missing owner/approver/ticket, duplicate/overlap lookup, wrong KDC source, old/new 4769 versions, duplicate transport, late arrival, and search-head restart. Assert all output and raw identity fields.

In the lab, compare Splunk output with Event Viewer and application/front-end/backend logs at the same instant. Prove that the approved KCD and RBCD flows produce the expected tuple, a deliberately absent lab approval returns one row, and publishing a valid row suppresses only notification. Remove lab delegation and confirm AD configuration restoration. Never create or broaden production delegation solely for a test.

Load-test peak 4769 rates, lookup size, search runtime, bundle distribution, scheduler concurrency, and index volume. Keep filtering in the base search, but do not drop relevant 4769 at ingest unless a separately retained raw tier and replay path have been approved.

## Step 6 — Investigate an unapproved path

Alert text should state `Unapproved Kerberos constrained-delegation path on <KDC>: <transited_services> -> <service_name> from <client_address> for <delegated_user>`. Include event/index time, record ID/version, service SID, status, ticket options/encryption, logon GUID/hashes when present, first/last seen, KDC health, approval state, AD inventory revision, asset/application owners, and runbook.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify raw 4769 XML, success status, nonempty transited services, exact normalization, KDC/source health, event identity, and lookup revision/uniqueness.
2. Resolve service/SPNs, account SIDs, and client address through authoritative AD, DNS/IPAM, CMDB, load-balancer, and application ownership; preserve raw values.
3. Inspect classic KCD and RBCD configuration on the actual front-end/backend accounts, including who can modify those objects and recent 5136 directory-change evidence where separately collected.
4. Confirm an approved deployment, failover, maintenance, service-account rotation, or support test with exact path and time. Do not accept an after-the-fact broad approval without owner/security review.
5. Correlate KDC 4768/4769/4624/4648 evidence and front-end/backend application/access logs. Remember that 4769 proves ticket issuance, not backend acceptance or data access.
6. If unauthorized, follow identity incident procedure to contain the service/account/host, preserve tickets/logs, and remove or narrow delegation through reviewed AD change.
7. Validate current AD configuration, approved application function, new 4769 behavior, backend access, and no unexpected alternate paths before closure.

Never automatically disable an account, delete an SPN, clear `msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo`, rewrite an RBCD descriptor, stop a KDC/service, isolate a server, or block a client from this result alone. These actions can break authentication and require AD/application ownership.

## Step 7 — False positives, dashboard, and evidence

Apply only the exact lookup contract in `knownFalsePositives`. Approval suppresses the alert row in the primary result but never raw storage, path-usage reporting, source health, lookup health, AD-configuration-change monitoring, or expired-path review. Record the lookup revision/hash and effective row used for every decision.

Build the dashboard described above. Distinguish requested service account from an SPN and from a resolved backend host. Label graph edges as observed KDC ticket paths, not network sessions. Display UTC or explicit timezone and place missing KDCs/extraction defects above findings. Review approved paths with no use for 90 days as candidates, but require application confirmation before removal.

Retain events and governance evidence under security/legal policy. Delegated usernames and service paths can be sensitive; restrict lookup/dashboard/export access and avoid unnecessary personal-data enrichment. This UC contributes technical evidence but does not attest compliance.

## Step 8 — Troubleshoot and maintain

- **No populated TransitedServices:** verify KCD/RBCD actually used S4U2proxy, KDC success auditing, event version/raw XML, source/type, add-on extraction, and application fallback. Do not infer delegation from volume.
- **All paths are unapproved:** check lookup existence/permissions, exact field names, normalization, bundle checksum, duplicate validation, effective epoch, and search peer. Never change the SPL to `inputlookup`-only matching without raw parity.
- **All paths are approved unexpectedly:** test a deliberately absent tuple and audit wildcard/blank/duplicate rows. Confirm lookup field order and `OUTPUTNEW` values.
- **Client address is loopback, proxy, or NAT:** preserve it and redesign the identity contract using tested additional evidence; do not silently substitute DNS or frontend owner.
- **ServiceName is an account rather than service-class SPN:** expected in some 4769 rendering. Use the exact field plus AD SPN resolution and do not pretend it is `ldap/host`.
- **Mapped IPv6 mismatch:** verify only `::ffff:` normalization. Keep native IPv6 exact and lowercase.
- **CIM and raw counts differ:** inspect tags, event types, acceleration range, normalized field semantics, and add-on version. Keep raw Microsoft fields authoritative.
- **Lookup changed after the event:** evaluate against event-time effective history, not only today's state; preserve prior revisions.
- **Ticket issued but backend has no access log:** that does not negate 4769. Investigate acceptance/authorization separately.
- **Configuration looks valid but path is risky:** an AD permission is not security approval. Escalate broad delegation and review least privilege.

Review KDC inventory/auditing, OS schema versions, add-on extraction, path normalization, AD exports, lookup validity, schedule/delay/checkpoint, source and lookup health, alert routing, dashboard, retention, and runbook quarterly and after domain, KDC, application, SPN, service-account, network, delegation, Windows, or Splunk changes. Keep `status=draft` until identity/Kerberos, application, and Splunk owners execute and sign the tests.
grandmaExplanation: Some business services are allowed to act for a person when they call another service. We compare each real use of that special trust with an approved path and warn when a new, expired, or incomplete path appears.
